subject: Clarify Redwood retention defaults for requests / prompts / generated outputs

Subject: Default retention windows for requests / prompts / outputs (SOC2 ask)

Hi Vanessa,

We're preparing for BrightBank's SOC2 readiness review and our auditor asked for a clear statement of Redwood's default capture and deletion behavior. Specific asks:
- What does Redwood keep by default for API "requests" (raw prompts, caller metadata) vs. "generated outputs" (model responses)?
- Default retention windows and any tiering (short/standard/long).
- How deletion/expunge requests are handled (turnaround SLA + audit trail).
- If data residency differs by account/region.

Can you send a short summary we can hand to the audit team? Ideally a PDF we can attach to our evidence packet. Deadline: EOD Nov 17.

Thanks,
Liam

Director, Platform Security
BrightBank

Hi Liam — thanks for the note and the deadline. High level first; attaching a short playbook (redwood_retention_playbook.pdf) and an internal diagram for our ops runbook.

Summary (short):
- Classification: Redwood treats incoming text prompts and the model-generated outputs as captured artifacts by default. Metadata (request IDs, timestamps, route/model used) are captured by default for observability.
- Default retention tiers (applies to Hosted API unless customer configures otherwise):
  * Short: 30 days — minimal capture (request metadata only; payload suppressed).
  * Standard (default): 90 days — full request/response payloads retained to support troubleshooting, quality monitoring, and regressions.
  * Long: 365 days — optional for customers with explicit retention contracts or archived evidence for audits.
- Deletion & expunge: Customers can request ad-hoc purge of captured artifacts via the Console or API. Typical SLA: we acknowledge within 24 hours and complete backend expunge within 72 hours for Hosted accounts; private/dedicated deployments follow the customer's control plane policy. Every purge action is tracked in an audit log entry (who/when/what).
- Residency: Data stored in the region tied to the customer's account by default; when a customer requests multi-region replication or cross-region failover, that is documented in the account's configuration and flagged in the audit evidence.

I'll loop in our infra lead for the technical nitty-gritty (exact indexing/TTL mechanics). If this summary works, I'll produce a short PDF you can attach.

Vanessa / Kim — internal technical note to include in the playbook (feel free to redact for customer PDF as needed):

- Implementation detail: Hosted API captures three logical artifacts:
  1) Observability metadata (latency, model, route, token counts) — retained as "index records" and kept for 365 days in the metrics store by default.
  2) Raw payload snapshot (request text/prompt + model generated content) — captured when the account has "full capture" enabled (Standard or Long tier). Default TTL for raw payloads is 90 days (Standard).
  3) Derivatives (embeddings, logs for quality monitoring, evals) — retention follows the account's capture setting; ephemeral copies used for caching are evicted per workload policy.

- Default suppression: For Short tier we redact full payloads at ingestion (store token counts + routing metadata only).

- Purge flow: purge requests call an internal expunge job which: 1) marks artifacts tombstoned; 2) deletes blob references from the active store; 3) garbage collects cold storage in the next scheduled GC window. We target complete artifact removal from all searchable systems in <=72 hours; full physical removal from backups may take longer and is represented in the audit trail.

- Residency nuance: In multi-tenant Hosted accounts, payloads live in the customer's region unless the customer has cross-region failover enabled; Dedicated & Private deployments control residency via customer-managed VPCs.

I'll drop a one-page technical appendix into the playbook before we hand it to BrightBank.

Hi Liam — attaching the finalized evidence packet per your ask. Key commitments again (so you have a one-paragraph statement for the auditor):

1) Default capture and windows (Hosted API):
   - Standard (default): full request + generated output payloads retained for 90 days (used for troubleshooting and quality monitoring).
   - Short (optional): payloads redacted, metadata retained for 30 days.
   - Long (customer contract): payloads retained up to 365 days if explicitly requested.

2) Deletion guarantees: on-demand purge requests submitted by the customer are acknowledged within 24 hours and completed in the hosted backend within 72 hours; each purge produces an immutable audit entry with timestamps and actor.

3) Residency: data is stored in the region tied to the customer's account by default; Dedicated/Private options give customers exclusive control over physical residency.

We've attached: redwood_retention_playbook.pdf (one-page summary + appendix), retention_workflow_diagram.png (ops flow), SOC2_evidence_req.pdf (your original request). Also included a HubSpot evidence link and DocuSign envelope reference in case you want an auditable handoff.
